To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elongation factors and aminoacyl tRNA synthetases are heterogeneously and noncovalently bound to high molecular weight complexes in postribosomal cell fractions, and that the complexes may contain more than one synthetase.
the aminoacyl transferase activity of leucyl tRNA synthetase is not a property of the synthetase itself but is a result of the association of the synthetases with elongation factors 1 or 2.

elongation factors 1, 2, and most of the aminoacyl tRNA synthetases exist in rat liver and cultured mammalian cells as high molecular weight protein aggregates, whereas only small amounts of the enzymes are found in their free, unaggregated forms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the role of the synthetases in the elongation process?
the following questions: What are the properties of the aminoacyl transferase and aminoacyl tRNA synthetase complexes, and how do these properties relate to the properties of the free enzymes?
the question of the existence of a complex between aminoacyl-tRNAs and aminoacyl transferase and/or aminoacyl-t-RNA synthetases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aminoacyl-tRNAsynthetases are present in the cell in a free, noncomplex form and also in association with other enzymes, e.g. elongation factor-1, elongation factor-2 and probably other enzymes.
the aminoacyl transferase activity and the synthetase activities are heterogeneously and nonuniformly distributed in the cell and in the ribosomes.
the synthetases and EF-1 and -2 are present in a complex form in the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elongation factors and the aminoacyl transferase enzymes are present in a number of complexes of various sizes, ranging from 10–26S to more than 3 million.
the aminoacyl transferase and aminoacyl tRNA synthetase enzymes are heterogeneously associated with the polysomal fraction and with the free ribosomes.
the elongation factors 1–2 are associated with the aminoacyl transferase system in rat liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EF-2 and EF-1 and the synthetases form high molecular weight aggregates in the cell.
aminoacyl tRNA synthetases and elongation factors are heterogeneously and extensively aggregated in the cell and that the free enzymes are a small fraction of the total cellular enzyme activity.
the synthetases and elongation factors are heterogeneously associated in the cell and that the synthetase-elongation factor complexes are not stable during cell disruption.
